summaries.summary: Human language comprehension involves partially identified cognitive processes, with EEG and ERPs used to study meaning integration across words.
Six ERP components from BIBREF0 are analyzed, and a pretrained neural network language model is proposed to probe features driving ERPs and comprehension.
ERP components are baseline-relative electrical responses named by polarity, timing, and scalp distribution, with N400, P600, PNP, EPNP, LAN, and ELAN introduced.
Related work links surprisal, distance, LSTM, RNNG, and recurrent neural networks to ERPs or MEG, while this work directly predicts ERPs without a linking function.
All six ERP components from BIBREF0 are predicted above chance by a pretrained language model, including P600 prediction from an LSTM.
Multitask learning shows shared information between ERP components and behavioral data, potentially clarifying ERP drivers and human language comprehension processes.
ERP components are predicted from fine-tuned language models, multitask learning reveals expected and surprising relationships, and heterogeneous behavioral and neural data share information.
The authors thank reviewers and acknowledge support in part by National Institutes of Health grant number U01NS098969.

Appendix visualizations and supplemental multitask variants show worse results without bi-LSTM encoders, qualitatively similar relationships, and Pearson correlations differing from joint-training benefits.
